references.text: The project is being renamed after its menu-bar app, **Khuluma** (isiNdebele and isiZulu for "speak"; it was called Lowkey until v0.11). Current work and decisions are in [`LOG.md`](LOG.md); the previous detailed plan is [archived](docs/archive/KHULUMA_RENAME_ROADMAP.md). Until the rename is done, the project has three parts:

references.text: - **Khuluma** (`tmux-whisperd/Sources/Khuluma`): the menu-bar app you dictate with. It owns the hotkey, the microphone, the sounds, delivery (paste, optionally send) and the Stats window. It transcribes over the daemon's socket and cleans the text up in Swift.
references.file_treatment: Update active operational names/paths/commands; preserve dated history and technical terms with narrow exceptions.

references.text: - **`tmux-whisperd`**: the local Parakeet daemon that keeps the model loaded.

references.text: - **The `tmux-whisper` CLI** (`bin/`): Khuluma's back end for now. It holds config, vocab, history and usage, starts and warms the daemon, and transcribes audio files. Khuluma calls it through a small set of JSON commands ([`docs/CLI_CONTRACTS.md`](docs/CLI_CONTRACTS.md)).
references.file_treatment: Update active operational names/paths/commands; preserve dated history and technical terms with narrow exceptions.

references.text: - A Parakeet CoreML model on disk, at `~/.local/share/tmux-whisper/models/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-coreml` (or `-v2-coreml`), or anywhere `swift_parakeet.model_path` in the config points. Install doesn't download it; FluidInference publishes these CoreML conversions on Hugging Face.

references.text: A checkout is separate from the installed app and daemon. `tools/build-khuluma-app.sh` builds from `tmux-whisperd/.build/` and installs `~/Applications/Khuluma.app`; the CLI's default installed daemon is `~/.local/share/tmux-whisper/native/tmux-whisperd/.build/release/tmux-whisperd`. Config or environment overrides may change daemon paths. Preserve build trees, models and caches during documentation housekeeping. The install and build commands below change the runtime; they are not documentation checks.

references.text: **Upgrading from Lowkey.app:** the first `build-khuluma-app.sh` quits `~/Applications/Lowkey.app`, moves it to the Trash and installs `Khuluma.app`. references.text: - **Lowkey phase 3c-1 (part 1): the daemon has one lifecycle and every take is visible**:

references.text: - **One daemon, always the right meta.** Starting or replacing `tmux-whisperd` (CLI fallbacks, warmups, installer refreshes) now happens under one per-socket kernel lock (`flock` on `<socket>.lifecycle.lock`, released automatically if its holder dies), with a recheck after acquiring it. A daemon that doesn't answer within 20 s of launch is stopped before the lock is released, so it can't come up later beside another. Before, concurrent callers could each launch a daemon and the meta file could name the one that lost (it did in 3 of 3 concurrent test runs). The meta is written atomically, and only once the daemon answering pings is the one just launched.
references.file_treatment: Preserve past releases; add verified new rename release entry only.

references.text: - **A live socket is never deleted.** The CLI no longer removes the socket before launching: the daemon itself replaces a socket nobody accepts on, and a daemon that accepts but doesn't answer (hung) is left alone rather than doubled. Pings time out after 5 s (`DICTATE_SWIFT_PARAKEET_PING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) instead of the 600 s transcription timeout.

references.text: - **Lowkey takes are visible from hotkey to delivery.** Lowkey publishes its marker before capture starts and moves it through `phase=recording|queued|processing|cli` until the take is delivered, fails or is cancelled. Before, only processing was visible, so an install could swap the daemon while you were still speaking. The CLI's idle check now counts only markers whose owner is alive and removes dead ones (it used to treat any file as busy forever). SwiftBar counts only the processing phases, `tmux-whisper cancel` no longer deletes Lowkey's markers, and Lowkey sweeps markers left by a crashed run at launch.

references.text: - **`tmux-whisper warmup --json`** starts the daemon if needed, loads the model and reports the truth: `ready` (the daemon reports this exact model path and version loaded), `warming` (being built or started elsewhere, or replaced and still cold) or `unavailable` (no model, no binary, start or load failed, or a build that failed in the last 10 minutes). Unlike `--best-effort`, it never claims success when nothing was preloaded, and it never builds inline. The daemon reports the model its engine actually holds, updated the moment a load commits.

references.text: - **Supervision.** At launch, on wake from sleep, at every recording start and when a take finds the daemon unreachable, Lowkey pings it (250 ms). If the daemon doesn't hold the configured model, Lowkey asks the CLI to start and warm it (`warmup --json`), so the CLI's lifecycle lock still owns every start. A warm daemon costs one ping and no CLI. Measured: with the daemon stopped, a Lowkey launch had it serving with the model loaded about 4 s later. One check runs at a time; failures back off 30 s → 2 min → 10 min, and a build in progress is rechecked every 30 s for up to 10 minutes. The menu shows `Parakeet: ready | warming up | unavailable`. It turns itself off for a CLI without the 0.11 capabilities, and with `[app] supervise_daemon = false`.

references.text: - **`tools/lowkey-report.sh`** summarises the log without printing any dictated text: outcomes, fallback and failure rates, warm overhead (stop → delivered minus Parakeet and delivery waits) as median/p90 by take length, a per-stage breakdown (including WAV prep plus request time minus model time on warm takes, the plan's trigger for moving the model in-process), cold takes, hotkey → first audio, Lowkey-started model warmups, and verify results per day. It judges each verify line only by the status right after the take id, since mismatch lines quote dictated text, and it leaves out takes missing the daemon's time for any pass. It ends with the v0.10.0 gates: 20+ warm native takes with median overhead under 100 ms, and 2+ days of verified takes with no mismatches. `--since`/`--days` narrow the window, and `--system` adds a memory spot check (pressure level, swap, compressor, daemon and Lowkey RSS). Takes logged before this change are summarised separately.

references.text: - **Lowkey: dictation works again after switching microphones or headphones**: after an input device change while idle, every hotkey press played the start chime and did nothing else, until the device changed back. The engine kept the old device's format, so AVAudioEngine raised an Objective-C exception when the tap was installed. Swift can't catch that, and HIToolbox silently swallowed it inside the hotkey handler, so nothing was logged and each press left an `inline-lowkey-*` marker behind. Those markers kept the CLI's idle check busy (blocking daemon upgrades) until Lowkey restarted.

references.text: - AVAudioEngine's Objective-C exceptions are caught and reported as errors (new `LowkeyObjC` target). A failed start always removes its marker, and a press during a start is ignored instead of stacking a second start.

references.text: - **Lowkey: autosend no longer sometimes pastes without sending in the Claude desktop app**: Lowkey posted Return 35 ms after Cmd+V (`send_delay_ms`). The CLI's two `osascript` runs had added ~80 ms of launch time on top of that. Back to back, Electron apps sometimes handle Return before the paste (Cmd+V goes through their Edit menu), so the text was pasted but not sent. The gap is now at least 150 ms; longer `send_delay_ms` values are kept.

references.text: - **Lowkey (experimental native app, phase 2 of #30)**: a signed menu-bar app that runs beside the CLI/Raycast setup. It owns the latency-critical path natively: a Carbon global hotkey (toggle, default `ctrl+option+space`, set with `[app] hotkey` in config.toml), AVAudioEngine capture at 16 kHz, preloaded AVAudioPlayer sounds (the start chime no longer waits on an `afplay` process), and paste/send via CGEvent with the same paste-target and send-mode settings as inline dictation. Transcription, cleanup, history, and usage stay in the CLI, so output is identical to today's inline dictation. Timings (hotkey→chime, engine start, hotkey→first audio, processing, delivery) are logged to `~/Library/Logs/Lowkey/app.log`.

references.text: - **New repo, archive the old one** (recommended; confirm in phase 0) rather than renaming `ricardo-nth/tmux-whisper` in place. Khuluma moves to `ricardo-nth/khuluma` with its history (`git filter-repo` on `tmux-whisperd/`, `docs/plans/KHULUMA_*`, `docs/plans/archive/LOWKEY_*`, `tools/*khuluma*`). The old repo gets a final CLI release and is archived. Archive URLs (Homebrew formula, `bootstrap.sh`, release tarballs) keep working without depending on rename redirects, and an archived repo can't be confused with the live product. The cost: issues, stars and watchers stay behind (transfer the open ones). Renaming in place keeps them, but then there's no repo to archive, and the redirects break if anything is ever created under the old name. GitHub doesn't promise that rename redirects cover tag archives or `raw.githubusercontent.com` links, which are exactly what the formula and `bootstrap.sh` use ([gh-rename]). Archiving makes code, releases, issues and PRs read-only, and doesn't close open issues ([gh-archive]).

TCC identifies an app by bundle id **plus** its code requirement, and the self-signed requirement very likely won't match a Developer ID signature ([tcc-identity], [tn2206], [dts-tcc]). references.text: In-process ownership (the original 3c) would save ~10–20 ms per take (WAV write/read, socket hop). references.text: A window opened from the Lowkey menu that makes dictating feel rewarding: totals, words per minute, a streak, records and an activity heatmap. Every number is either **measured** or **labelled as an estimate with its assumption shown**. Stats store counts and durations only, never what was said.
references.file_treatment: Preserve dated evidence; classify legacy names. Archive index links may be repaired without rewriting historical claims.

references.text: 1. **Lowkey's CLI fallback counts takes it may not deliver.** With `INLINE_DELIVERY_MODE=external`, `inline process` records usage (`bin/tmux-whisper:6387`) *before* Lowkey pastes (`processWithCLI`, `AppController.swift`). A paste failure still earns a dictation, words and a streak day. Fixed in stage 1 (deferred usage).
references.file_treatment: Preserve dated evidence; classify legacy names. Archive index links may be repaired without rewriting historical claims.

references.text: 4. **Dictating with the stats window in front.** Inline `paste_target` defaults to `current` (`config.sh:269`), so a take delivered while Stats is frontmost would paste and send into Lowkey and still count. This can also happen when Stats is opened *during* a take. The guard belongs at delivery, not only at start.
references.file_treatment: Preserve dated evidence; classify legacy names. Archive index links may be repaired without rewriting historical claims.

references.text: - **Day key = the Gregorian local date at delivery.** Lowkey sends `delivered_local_date` (computed at the moment of delivery, Gregorian calendar, system time zone) in `TakeRecord`, so a replay days later lands on the right day. The tmux and CLI-inline flows write at delivery, so they use `now()` in local time. `DICTATE_USAGE_NOW` plus `TZ` drive tests. Travel can move a take to a neighbouring day; that's documented. `started_at` and the day key come from the same instant.

references.text: - **Older writers are safe.** The current writer loads, mutates and dumps the whole document (`history.sh:335–367`), so it preserves the new keys verbatim but doesn't update them. Those deliveries show up as `untracked_deliveries`. The test uses the **real previous writer** (`git show origin/main:bin/tmux-whisper-lib/history.sh`), not a simulation.

references.text: - **Lowkey CLI fallback (deferred usage):** new capability `deferred_usage`. `inline process … --defer-usage` skips the ledger (history and bench as today). After delivery, Lowkey sends `inline record` with `"usage_only": true` and the real outcome and delivery time, with the delivered text so the CLI keeps owning the word count. That records usage once (by take id) and writes no second history or bench row. Without the capability (an older CLI), behaviour is today's, documented as legacy.

references.text: - Durable persistence: each take's record is spooled to `~/Library/Application Support/Lowkey/pending/` before `inline record` runs and removed once the CLI has taken it. Quit waits up to 20 s for the take in progress and the queue; anything left (quit timeout, crash, failing CLI) replays at the next launch, and `inline record` keeps a ledger of take IDs (`.cache/recorded-takes`) so a replay never counts usage twice. Partial acknowledgements (usage or history not saved) are logged, not retried.
